items.sentenceAfter: manger de la pizza ce soir.
items.fullSentence: Je vais manger de la pizza ce soir.
items.sentenceTrans: I'm going to eat pizza this evening.

whyWrong.vas: That's the tu form — je vais.
whyWrong.va: That's the il/elle form — je vais.
whyWrong.allons: That's the nous form — je vais.

items.fullSentence: Nous allons cuisiner ensemble cette semaine.
items.sentenceTrans: We're going to cook together this week.

whyWrong.va: That's the singular il form — nous allons.
whyWrong.vont: That's the ils form — nous allons.
whyWrong.allez: That's the vous form — nous allons.

items.sentenceTrans: What are you going to order?

whyWrong.allons: That's the nous form — vous allez.
whyWrong.vont: That's the ils form — vous allez.
whyWrong.va: That's the il form — vous allez.

items.fullSentence: Je ne vais pas manger de viande ce soir.
items.sentenceTrans: I'm not going to eat meat this evening.

whyWrong.mange: After 'vais' you use the infinitive manger, not the conjugated form.
whyWrong.manges: That's a conjugated tu form; after aller you need the infinitive manger.
whyWrong.mangé: That's the past participle; the near future takes the infinitive manger.

whyWrong.vas: 'tu vas manger' means 'you're going to eat', not 'you must'.

whyWrong.faut: faut is impersonal — it only ever takes il ('il faut'); with nous it's devons.
whyWrong.devez: That's the vous form — nous devons.

whyWrong.va: 'elle va cuisiner' means 'she's going to cook', not 'she can'.
whyWrong.faut: faut is impersonal ('il faut'); it can't take 'elle' as its subject.

items.sentenceTrans: Are you going to drink some coffee?

whyWrong.va: va is the il/elle form — tu vas.
whyWrong.vais: vais is the je form — tu vas.
whyWrong.allez: allez is the vous form — tu vas.

items.fullSentence: Ils vont faire les courses demain.
items.sentenceTrans: They're going to do the shopping tomorrow.

whyWrong.allons: allons is the nous form — ils vont.
whyWrong.allez: allez is the vous form — ils vont.

items.fullSentence: Pour rester en bonne santé, il faut manger équilibré.
items.sentenceTrans: To stay healthy, you need to eat a balanced diet.

whyWrong.tu peux: 'You can' — the sentence states a necessity: il faut.
whyWrong.tu devrais: 'You should' (conditional) — a general necessity is il faut.
whyWrong.il devrait: 'It should' — the set phrase for necessity is il faut.
